correctness.rationale: Exact Dirichlet density, Jacobian 2, half-angle identity, strict feasibility of the unique zero and derivative bounds all reconstruct algebraically. The clipped arcsine threshold is exact for 0<t<4; dominated convergence over the diamond with H>=1 gives the coefficient, and the inverse map density converges in L1 by Scheffe, implying marked total variation. Upper and lower transverse constants are witnessed by square and degenerate configurations. Standard-library numerical checks of 16,000 gap samples, integral quadrature and Monte Carlo all passed; none substitutes for the analytic derivation. No unproved extrapolation from finite tests is used.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Finch covers the same sampling law but its inspected results are side and angle distributions, not the law of an alternating four-side sum. Quadrilateral area/perimeter moments and angle-conditioned area laws cannot recover a signed Pitot-residual near-zero conditional measure. Izmestiev studies a deterministic porism rather than the indicated probability. The separately inspected cyclic-quadrilateral area/side-variance stability theorem fixes different symmetric side parameters and controls area, not the alternating signed side sum; it does not imply the marked near-incircle law.

The single-edge facet/clearance criterion samples inside a fixed polytope and cannot imply random-circle sample shape statistics.

value.rationale: The Pitot defect has an intrinsic and mathematically motivated meaning as the exact incircle feasibility obstruction for cyclic quadrilaterals. A global normal coordinate with optimal stability constants quantifies near-feasibility; the exact all-threshold probability and marked total-variation limit describe prevalence and geometry of near-tangential shapes. These are natural shape-statistical questions not implied by the deterministic Pitot equality or currently inspected distribution tables.
